articles.title: My husband has such bad breath we haven’t kissed in years – but he won’t see a dentist | Ask Annalisa Barbieri
articles.summary: You clearly love him, but do you love yourself enough to stop letting him get away with this? I’ ve got a very upsetting problem in my marriage: my husband has extremely bad breath. We have been together for 20 years and it has always been noticeable, but has got worse in recent years.
body: I have spoken to him about this issue in the past, and even managed to get him to the dentist once, but he became so frightened that he ran out of the surgery. Since then, whenever I mention his breath or the dentist, he becomes very defensive.
I feel embarrassed when he is talking to other people because I know they can smell it too.

We haven’t kissed in years as the thought of kissing makes me feel sick. He often complains that I don’t initiate sex, and asks why I’m not more affectionate towards him. The truth is that his breath puts me off. I don’t want to hurt him by saying this, but it is becoming increasingly difficult for me to feel physically close to him.
I know his fear of the dentist is real. I don’t want to shame him or make him feel unattractive. But I also feel frustrated because I have tried to help him and he simply won’t address it.
points: You clearly love him, but do you love yourself enough to stop letting him get away with this?

articles.title: Hacks, AI and conspiracy theories: why are we having so many outages?
articles.summary: After chaos at airlines, banks and companies from Microsoft to Apple, people have become convinced the world’s systems are under attack. Nicole Reindorf’s American Airlines flight was ready for takeoff in Phoenix when the pilot came on the intercom and announced what was to become the longest…
body: Reindorf, 70, had seen the headlines hours before about a global Microsoft outage. She immediately suspected the two were linked in some way by AI-related threats – and that she would not get to the wedding of her best friend’s son in California.
“I presumed there had been a hack of the aviation system and that it would be down for days,” she said.

Instead, flights resumed later that day and Reindorf was able to make the wedding even if she missed that night’s rehearsal dinner. But passengers appeared to be convinced of two things, she said: “That it was a cyber-attack and that we were not going to be told the truth about it.”

This was not an isolated view. What happened in the days after the incident, which began on Thursday 12 November, left many wondering if the US, and the western world, was under a coordinated assault. By Tuesday big US banks, Apple, and the National Security Agency had also been affected by technical glitches. Researchers also flagged a cyber-attack that targeted 178 organisations worldwide, although the financial losses appeared to be small.
points: After chaos at airlines, banks and companies from Microsoft to Apple, people have become convinced the world’s systems are under attack.

articles.title: Why I love Madrid in winter: ‘Locals get into the spirit by doing their shopping in novelty hats’
articles.summary: The streets and squares of the Spanish capital come alive with Madrileños shopping, drinking and dining outdoors, warmed by lap blankets and patio heaters. Live in Madrid long enough and you hear the same weather-related proverbs again and again.
body: It’s nice to see the Christmas lights up close, especially where they’re themed and art-directed by guest designers across the facade of the Four Seasons hotel and the flagship store of Spanish leatherware brand Loewe. But it’s often better to get a little distance, and El Cielo de Montera is my favourite of the city’s competing roof terraces. With the Gran Vía below and the glowing blue art deco clock of the Telefónica building above, winter in Madrid looks a little like 1930s Manhattan from this angle.

Civic life continues outdoors, and there’s great sensory pleasure to dining in the cold air under lap blankets and patio heaters, though I also love the huddled feel of retreating deep inside a vintage tavern. Mulled wine isn’t a big thing in Spain but they do a good one at Vinícola Mentridana, an atmospheric bodega, and if you think of sherry as a winter drink, at the beautifully basic La Venencia it’s the only thing that has been served since 1922. There are five varieties poured straight from the casks.

articles.title: This is how we do it: ‘One time my son said: “I heard you having sex. It was disgusting.” That killed the vibe’
articles.summary: Empty nesters Anna and Richard have found the freedom and space to experiment with intimacy. • How do you do it? Share the story of your sex life, anonymously. I’m a much more active participant sexually now. I used to be more reactive.
body: I’ve learned that sex can get better with age and time. Last year, our children left home to go to university, and that has made a big difference. There were times when the kids were at home and thought they heard Richard and me having sex. I remember my son told us it was a traumatic experience, which made me not want to do it.
I couldn’t be in the moment because I was worried: are the kids going to come home? Will they hear us? Then I felt guilty because we wouldn’t be having as much sex.

But I’m older now, and I have a little bit more life experience, especially being in a relationship with someone for 23 years. We’ve been to couples’ therapy and have learned how to better manage conflict. In the past, I felt Richard would shut down difficult subjects, which made me feel that I couldn’t ask for things, like support with the kids. I felt that I’d lost a sense of control in the relationship. But we were able to identify the areas where we needed help and built trust. That leads into our sexual relationship.

articles.title: How to Spend 3 Perfect Days in Naples
articles.summary: From archaeological must-sees to the best places for sipping a spritz, according to someone who has known the city for decades.
body: A fascinating, complex, and multi-layered city, Naples is brimming with contradictions. Dilapidated, neglected neighborhoods share city space with splendid palaces and world-beating museums. The city’s origins go back to the ancient Greeks, yet the contemporary art scene here is buzzing. There is a state-of-the-art metro system designed by renowned artists and architects (no wonder, since the traffic is infamously heavy).

I’ve been visiting for over 30 years and have seen huge changes, most of them positive. Naples today is safer, more tourist-friendly, and cleaner than ever before, yet it remains Italy’s most beguiling city. The eating and drinking scene has evolved, there is a much wider choice of places to stay (with Rocco Forte due to open a hotel here in 2027), and museums and monuments have been spruced up and reorganized. In 2027, the America’s Cup will arrive as well.

You could easily spend two weeks in Naples and not see everything. But if you only have three days, start early and be prepared to pack in as much as possible; you can rest once you get home. Here is my advice for how to make the most of it.
points: From archaeological must-sees to the best places for sipping a spritz, according to someone who has known the city for decades.

articles.title: 11 Warm-Weather Destinations to Flock to This Winter
articles.summary: Trade your snow boots for flip-flops at these sunny locations across the globe.
body: Arguably the best way to overcome winter is to pretend like it’s not happening—i.e., jetting off to a warm-weather destination, where seasons are not taken very seriously and an outdoor adventure is always on the table. The best winter vacation destinations offer comfortable temperatures, off-peak advantages, and festive happenings. On this list, you’ll find some of the usual suspects, from Punta Cana to the US Virgin Islands, as well as locales you might not have considered (far too often, travelers forget vibrant Marrakech is a shorter-haul Mediterranean option).

Whether you’re interested in hiking to the wild and wondrous waterfalls of Puerto Rico’s El Yunque National Rainforest, snorkeling through the kaleidoscopic waters of Belize’s barrier reef, or simply want to kick back and relax with a dip in Costa Rica’s hot springs, these sunny locations are bound to cure those cold-weather blues. So, trade your snow boots for flip-flops and get to plotting your next escape.

articles.title: 11 Best Airbnbs Near Acadia National Park for a Nature-Filled Vacation
articles.summary: The best Airbnbs near Acadia National Park put you right in the middle of its coastal landscape; here are our favorite ones.
body: The American West may play host to the lion’s share of iconic national parks —Yosemite, Yellowstone, Grand Canyon—but Acadia National Park is the crown jewel of the East Coast. Despite being one of the most compact national parks in the country, it’s also one of the most frequented, with around four million visitors a year who journey here to experience its historic carriage roads and the rugged Atlantic coast.

If you’re searching for a place to stay in proximity to the region’s dense forests and craggy coastlines, start by looking at the best Airbnbs near Acadia National Park. Offering more flexibility than a hotel—plus the possibility for true off-the-grid stays—the best homes are surrounded by nature. Winter travelers will want to bookmark amenities like fire pits and freestanding soaking tubs that make for a particularly cozy trip.

articles.title: Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando Are Married!
articles.summary: The couple tied the knot in a poolside ceremony in Palm Springs surrounded by dramatic flowers after five years together.
body: On Saturday, November 21, Miley Cyrus married Maxx Morando —poolside in Palm Springs, with the ceremony officiated by the Flaming Lips’ Wayne Coyne. Congratulations to the very happy rock stars!

33-year-old Cyrus and Morando, 28, tied the knot in front of an intimate crowd of family and friends, underneath a dramatic archway framed by white florals and candles. (Because when you can buy yourself flowers, why not buy out all of Hollywood’s florists for your nuptials?) Cyrus wore a draped long-sleeve white silk gown with a plunging back and long train, paired with pointed white pumps and a loose updo. Morando wore a simple black suit and corsage. In photos, Cyrus can be seen smiling brightly and wiping away tears as Morando shared his vows. Onlookers were dressed in all-black black-tie looks.

Cyrus’s mother Tish Cyrus and her partner Dominic Purcell, father Billy Ray and his partner Elizabeth Hurley, and her sister Noah were all in attendance. It was reported that the couple held their rehearsal the previous day.

articles.title: The 8 Best James Bond Films
articles.summary: As we await Robert Pattinson’s first outing as 007, these are the classics worth revisiting now.
body: Terrible puns. Rampant misogyny. Disposable female characters. A frequently stale rotation of vodka martinis, gun fights, and stiff-upper-lip bureaucracy. Bond movies are very easy to make fun of—and, let’s face it, of the 25 that have so far been released over the past six decades, a majority are pretty forgettable. But there are a handful that are worth watching, even if you actively abhor the subgenre.
Following Robert Pattinson’s appointment as the new 007, we present eight Bond films that are actually decent. May more follow!

Where it all began. A suave Sean Connery, Ursula Andress as the bikini-clad Honey Ryder, the pristine white beaches of Jamaica… this Terence Young-helmed first installment of the franchise laid the blueprint for everything that followed, but is also a thoroughly entertaining romp in its own right. It’s easy to see why it became a box-office bonanza and birthed a cultural phenomenon that endures to this day.
